Social Patterns and the Community - Social patterns involve the interaction of lives in the community, but they begin in smaller units such as the family. Coal development could affect the family in one or more of several ways.
The increased regular income could result in better housing, more adequate nutrition, children with more pride in themselves, their home and their family and, as result, more determination to acquire a better education and be prepared for better jobs. Improved habits could become part of the lives of the younger generation. Added facilities for health, education and other services would strengthen these effects.
On the other hand, increased income could provide a greater opportunity for alcoholism and socially undesirable behavior. Large-scale coal development could increase dependence by the Indian people on the royalty income, and this will greatly magnify the trauma when mining ceases and this income disappears.
The Indian communities which will be most affected are located along the Little Bighorn River from Hardin to Lodge Grass. If a large number of new people settled in these communities, the Indian people could become a minority in their own community. Some of the accompanying social and governmental changes could be undesireable to the Indian people. Since social values both influence and are influenced by the social patterns of a community, changes in these patterns brought about by an influx of new residents might be unacceptable to the long-time residents. This would bring about varying degrees of social stress until an accommodation of values and influence is established.
